question: Do both adapters hit the same media transports: inline base64 bytes as inlineData and a URL as fileData?

observation.note: Ran both sub-cases through the recording proxy so the wire part keys and fileUri forwarding are captured for the genai side, whether accepted or rejected.

uri.providerError: Resource has been exhausted (e.g. check quota).

observation.note: BOTH sub-cases ran through the recording proxy, so the wire part keys and fileUri forwarding are captured for the AI SDK side too.

finding: Inline base64: @google/genai accepted (wire part keys [inlineData]); AI SDK accepted (wire part keys [inlineData]). URI fileData TRANSPORT: @google/genai sent the URL on fileData.fileUri=true; AI SDK sent it on fileData.fileUri=true. URI fileData ENDPOINT-ACCEPTANCE: unproven in this run. Both sides got a 429 (genai) / 429 (ai-sdk), and a 429 cannot be attributed to the arbitrary fileUri host: the plain-text control call that succeeded afterwards (plainTextAccepted=true, HTTP 200) only rules out a general generate-content quota, never a separate media or file-URI quota. Control call (context only, not proof): plain text succeeded after the URI case genai=true (HTTP 200). The MediaBlock encoding:url -> fileData and encoding:base64 -> inlineData mapping in neutralConverters is transported unchanged by both adapters.
